requirements.title: SIZE defines the count of characters transferred by input data edit descriptors
requirements.definition: In an input statement, SIZE= causes the specified variable to become defined with the count of characters transferred from the file by data edit descriptors; blanks inserted as padding are not counted.

pending.size-defined-with-data-edit-character-co: Use nonadvancing formatted external input with SIZE initialized to -777, a known record such as "ABCDEF", and data edit descriptors that transfer a fixed number of characters; expect SIZE to equal that count after successful input.
pending.size-excludes-padding-blanks: Use a short external record with PAD="YES" and a field wider than the physical characters; initialize SIZE and target to nondefault sentinels and expect SIZE to count only real transferred characters, not inserted padding blanks.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or using a compile-only conforming control) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT or named status values where the standard names them, required INQUIRE tokens, or required diagnosis of a numbered syntax rule or constraint. Negative/source-control plans change one property from the conforming control and do not require a particular diagnostic message, severity, exit status, or printed rule number.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. IOMSG wording, processor-dependent numeric status values, external-file byte encodings, buffering, timing, and actual overlap of asynchronous operations are never an oracle. A diagnostic facet is only a future source-control plan when the cited numbered rule alone is violated and the invalid program reaches that rule.
requirements.dependencies: Registered dependencies: clauses 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, earlier clause 12 connection/access catalogues, and existing clause 13 format/editing catalogues for source form, names, labels, expressions, variables, units, access methods, internal files, formatting, and existing mode descriptors where used by pending controls. Unregistered dependencies explicitly retained: later 12.6 input/output-item rules; 12.7-12.11 transfer, status, INQUIRE, WAIT, and asynchronous semantics; clause 15 defined I/O; clause 16 named I/O status constants if future fixtures use them; clause 19 scope and lifetime controls.

requirements.title: SIZE definition timing depends on synchronous versus asynchronous input
requirements.definition: For a synchronous input statement, SIZE= definition occurs when execution of the statement completes; for an asynchronous input statement, definition occurs when the corresponding wait operation is performed.

pending.synchronous-size-defined-at-statement-co: After a synchronous nonadvancing READ with SIZE initialized to -777, inspect SIZE immediately after statement completion and expect the character count.
pending.asynchronous-size-defined-at-wait: For ASYNCHRONOUS="YES" input with SIZE initialized to -777, do not inspect SIZE until WAIT completes; after WAIT, expect the count. The plan avoids reading SIZE while its definition is pending.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.6.2.2-12.6.2.16, the individual io-control-spec specifiers (batch160). Every unit hash-verified by independent reviewers across two rounds. Each temporary mode specifier is split into its value restriction, its one-statement effect with restoration of the connection mode (observed by INQUIRE after the statement), and the omitted-means-unchanged rule. Round 1 found a pending plan expecting exact output from I2 on a positive value without fixing the sign mode; it now uses SS, and a sweep found no other plus-, leading-zero- or rounding-dependent exact output. R1215 and C1232 were pre-accounted. Source accounting only.
